steps.scene: You're approaching a level crossing with lights. The crossing is clear, then a steady amber light comes on.

question.prompt: What is that amber light telling you?

options.text: A train is coming — stop, unless you've already crossed the white line
Hurry across before the red lights start
Nothing yet — wait for red before you do anything

question.explanation: Steady amber is the first warning of a train. Flashing red lights follow it, and then the barriers come down.

steps.title: Flashing red means stop
steps.body: Flashing red lights at a level crossing mean stop before the barrier or stop line — whatever the barrier is doing.

question.prompt: The red lights start flashing as you approach a level crossing. What do you do?

options.text: Cross quickly, while the barrier is still up
Drive on, because you can't see a train yet

question.explanation: The lights come on well before the train does, and they mean stop. Never try to beat a barrier.

steps.title: One train can hide another
steps.body: If the lights keep flashing after a train has gone by, another one is coming. Carry on waiting until they stop.

question.prompt: A train passes, but the red lights keep flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Cross as soon as that train is out of sight

question.explanation: The lights stop when it's safe, not when the train has passed. A second train from the other way is exactly the danger.

steps.scene: You're already driving over a level crossing when the amber lights come on and a warning starts to sound.

options.text: Stop where you are and wait for the barrier
Keep going and clear the crossing
Reverse back the way you came

question.explanation: Once you're on the crossing the only safe direction is forward. Keep going and get clear of the rails.

steps.title: Stalled on the crossing
steps.prompt: Your car has stalled on a level crossing. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Get everyone out of the car and clear of the crossing
Use the railway telephone to tell the signal operator
Move the vehicle clear, if there's time and you're told you can
If the alarm sounds, leave the vehicle and get clear at once

steps.explanation: People first, then the phone, then the car — and the moment an alarm sounds, get off the crossing and stay off.

question.prompt: Three white boards with red diagonal bars, beside the road, mean…

options.text: You're approaching a concealed level crossing
A lay-by is coming up shortly

question.explanation: The bars count you down to a concealed level crossing: three, two, one. Be ready to stop when they run out.

steps.wrongBelief: As long as no lights are flashing, you can drive onto a level crossing.

options.text: It's right — no lights means the crossing is yours
The road beyond must be clear too, so you never stop on the rails
You must always stop first, then cross

question.explanation: It's the box-junction rule with far worse consequences: don't move on until you can drive straight off again.

steps.repairNote: Unlit or not, never drive onto a crossing until the far side is clear. Nothing should ever stop you on the rails.
